rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The $142M decline in operating cash flow was driven by combined working capital changes, with the inventory increase ($171.9M) being the single largest use of cash as stated in the cash flow discussion. The simultaneous receivables increase ($118.4M per cash flow statement) was also material but partially offset by a $154.5M accounts payable increase. The receivables buildup is consistent with the 19.8% international wholesale growth and 24.6% distributor sales growth, which carry credit terms, as shown in quarterly DSO signals. Management highlighted the primary driver (inventory) but the receivables increase is explained by the same revenue mix shift disclosed in segment data.
